description: AWS IAM Misconfiguration Scanner - Rule Definitions with MITRE ATT&CK mappings

rules.description: Root account does not have MFA enabled.
rules.remediation: Enable MFA on root account immediately.

mitre_attack.rationale: Root without MFA is a high-value valid cloud account. Compromised root credentials enable full account takeover without a second factor.

rules.description: IAM user has console access but no MFA enabled.

mitre_attack.rationale: Console users without MFA are easier targets for password-based initial access using valid cloud accounts.
Action:* Resource:* grants unrestricted privileges, enabling adversaries to use valid accounts for account manipulation and elevation of privileges.

rules.description: Access key has not been used for >90 days.

mitre_attack.rationale: Stale but active access keys are long-lived credentials that adversaries can reuse if leaked or stolen.

rules.description: Access key older than 90 days without rotation.

mitre_attack.rationale: Unrotated access keys increase the window of opportunity for credential theft and continued use of valid cloud accounts.
Wildcard inline policies create hard-to-audit admin-like privileges that support account manipulation and privilege abuse.

rules.description: Role trust policy allows any principal (*).

mitre_attack.rationale: A trust policy with Principal:* lets any identity assume the role, enabling initial access and abuse of cloud role privileges.

rules.description: Entity has permissions that can lead to privilege escalation.

mitre_attack.rationale: IAM actions such as CreatePolicyVersion, PassRole, AttachUserPolicy, and CreateAccessKey map directly to account manipulation and privilege escalation.

rules.description: Account password policy is too permissive.
rules.remediation: Enforce strong password policy (14+ chars, complexity, rotation).

mitre_attack.rationale: Weak password policies make online password guessing and credential stuffing against valid accounts more practical.

rules.description: Policies attached directly to users instead of groups.
rules.remediation: Use IAM groups for policy management.

mitre_attack.rationale: Direct user policy attachments increase privilege sprawl and make account manipulation harder to detect during audits.
Cross-account role trust without ExternalId is vulnerable to confused-deputy abuse of trusted relationships and cloud roles.

rules.description: Broad permissions granted without any Condition constraints.
rules.remediation: Add aws:SourceIp, MFA, or other conditions.

mitre_attack.rationale: Broad IAM/S3/EC2 permissions without conditions enable unrestricted discovery and collection from cloud resources once credentials are obtained.
